target.name: Polar Semiconductor

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $700M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median

methods.rationale: 13 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Polar Semiconductor is a Growth-stage chip design and manufacturing company that has raised $700M+ in total capital, including a 2024 recapitalization led by Niobrara Capital and Prysm Capital. The target operates within the Chips & Semiconductors sector, which includes 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers such as Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, and SambaNova Systems.

Of three valuation methods assessed, only Stage-Progression proved applicable. This method uses the $700M total raised as a proxy for current enterprise value and applies a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of Growth-stage advancement, yielding an implied valuation of $840M. Peer-Median analysis could not be applied due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables in the semiconductor cohort; while 13 same-sector peers exist, filtering for stage and valuation tier yielded fewer than three datapoints. Public-Comp Anchoring, though the sector median P/S multiple stands at 18.9x across the three public tickers, could not proceed without the target's revenue figure, which remains undisclosed.

The triangulation analysis supports a valuation range of $714M to $966M, with a median of $840M. This range reflects modest upside from the capital raised baseline. Key uncertainties include the absence of comparable transaction multiples for private Growth-stage semiconductor firms and lack of target revenue disclosure, both of which materially constrain precision. An updated valuation would benefit from either revenue guidance or identification of additional same-stage private comparables.
